- Appetite: Minor fluctuations; occasional increased chocolate consumption
- Motivation/Energy: Low energy; anhedonia; reduced interest in activities

Formulation:
- Predisposing factors: Family history of depression; female gender; baseline vulnerability to anxiety
- Precipitating factors: Start of a new, stressful job
- Perpetuating factors: Sleep disturbance, daytime fatigue, avoidance of social/recreational activities, constant worry
- Protective factors: Family support; willingness to pursue talking therapy

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce morning anxiety; improve sleep; maintain work functioning; re-engage in activities
- Clinical Goal(s): Within 4–6 weeks, reduce anxiety symptoms; improve sleep to 6–7 hours; resume social activities; initiate evidence-based therapy
- Actions (Patient): Attend referral to talking therapy; practice sleep hygiene; limit caffeine/alcohol; engage in gradual exposure to anxiety-provoking situations; maintain daily routine; track mood/sleep
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Provide NHS talking therapy referral; supply self-help resources; arrange baseline blood tests for palpitations; schedule GP follow-up in about 1 week after tests; provide sleep-improvement guidance

Secondary Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Improve mood and energy
- Clinical Goal(s): Within 6–8 weeks, improved mood and energy; return to regular activities
- Actions (Patient): Continue engagement with therapy; maintain routine; seek support as needed
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Monitor depressive symptoms; assess functional improvement; consider escalation if insufficient response; discuss pharmacotherapy if indicated

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention:
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Anxiety management, sleep hygiene, palpitations, pathway to talking therapy, self-help resources
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Worsening sleep, escalating worry, social withdrawal, inability to cope with daily tasks
- Coping Strategies: Breathing exercises, mindfulness/grounding techniques, regular physical activity, structured daily schedule, limiting caffeine/alcohol

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety — High: Onset after a major life stressor (new job); persistent work-related anxiety with impairment
- Major Depressive Disorder with anxious distress — Medium: Depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, sleep disruption; anxiety present; full criteria duration not fully established in transcript
- Generalized Anxiety Disorder — Medium: Chronic worry with autonomic arousal and sleep disturbance; duration not yet confirmed as DSM-5 threshold for GAD
